marks.gloss_en: if consecrating, vowing valuations, dedicating and separating tithes are barred on the festival, a fortiori on Shabbat
ומי אמר רבי יוחנן הכי? he holds the halakha follows a stam mishna, and the stam mishna bars consecrating on the festival, a fortiori on Shabbat
לא קשיא: here, obligations with a fixed time (the pesach -- now or never); there, obligations with no fixed time
R. Yochanan's own principle: the halakha follows an unattributed mishna
נימא מסייע ליה -- the erev-Pesach-on-Shabbat mishna has one take his lamb, seemingly consecrating it on Shabbat
a person may consecrate his Paschal lamb on Shabbat
הכא במאי עסקינן: registering others onto his own lamb, consecrated from the outset -- the mishna proves nothing about consecrating on Shabbat
the mishna speaks of one who registers others with him onto his own Paschal lamb -- the animal stands consecrated from the outset, so nothing is consecrated on Shabbat
והא אנן תנן: one may not register for an animal ab initio on the festival -- so even registration should be barred
שאני הכא -- a regular participant is as one registered from the outset
mishna: one may not register for an animal ab initio on the festival
והא תני רבי הושעיא -- one takes a lamb from his usual shepherd AND CONSECRATES IT, apparently on Shabbat itself
the shepherd, whom he frequents, consecrated it beforehand
against the counter 'but it teaches makdish!': that consecration is hekdesh illuy, a rabbinic valuation-addition, permitted on Shabbat by all
R. Hoshaya's baraita: one goes to a shepherd he frequents, who gives him a lamb for his pesach, and he consecrates it and fulfils his duty with it
